Sufganiyot (Hanukkah Jelly Doughnuts)

Served at: Hanukkah (Festival of Lights)

Makes about 12-15 doughnutsPrep 2 hours 30 min (includes rising time)Cook 20 min

Sufganiyot are delightful, deep-fried jelly doughnuts traditionally enjoyed during Hanukkah, the Jewish Festival of Lights. Their preparation, involving frying in oil, symbolizes and celebrates the miracle of the oil that lasted eight days in the Temple of Jerusalem. These fluffy, sweet treats are a joyous centerpiece for any Hanukkah celebration.

Ingredients

  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) warm milk (105-115°F / 40-46°C)
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons (7g) active dry yeast (one standard packet)
  • 1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar, plus 1 teaspoon
  • 2 1/2 cups (300g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 2 large eggs, at room temperature
  • 1/4 cup (56g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled
  • 4-6 cups (about 1-1.5 liters) vegetable oil, for frying
  • 1 cup (240g) strawberry or raspberry jam, for filling
  • 1/2 cup (60g) powdered sugar, for dusting

Method

  1. In a small bowl, combine the warm milk, 1 teaspoon of granulated sugar, and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, remaining 1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar, and salt.
  3. Add the proofed yeast mixture, eggs, and melted butter to the dry ingredients. Mix with a wooden spoon or stand mixer with a dough hook until a shaggy dough forms.
  4. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes, or use a stand mixer for 5-7 minutes, until the dough is smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky.
  5. Lightly grease a clean bowl with a little oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
  6. Once risen, gently punch down the dough. Turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and roll it out to about 1/2-inch (1.25 cm) thickness.
  7. Using a 2.5-3 inch (6-7.5 cm) round cookie cutter or a drinking glass, cut out circles of dough. Gather and re-roll scraps once to cut out more doughnuts. Place the cut doughnuts on a parchment-lined baking sheet, leaving some space between them.
  8. Cover the doughnuts loosely with plastic wrap or a clean towel and let them rise again in a warm place for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
  9. While the doughnuts are rising for the second time, heat the vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat to 350°F (175°C). Use a deep-fry thermometer to monitor the temperature.
  10. Carefully lower 2-3 doughnuts into the hot oil, being careful not to overcrowd the pot. Fry for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
  11. Using a slotted spoon or spider, remove the fried doughnuts and place them on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
  12. Once slightly cooled but still warm, fill the doughnuts. Use a piping bag fitted with a long, thin nozzle (or a clean pastry bag with a small corner snipped off) to inject about 1 tablespoon of jam into the side of each doughnut.
  13. Dust generously with powdered sugar before serving. Sufganiyot are best enjoyed warm on the day they are made.

Tips

  • Maintaining the oil temperature is crucial; if it's too low, the doughnuts will be greasy, and if too high, they'll brown too quickly on the outside and be raw inside.
  • For a richer flavor, you can add a teaspoon of vanilla extract or a pinch of nutmeg to the dough.
  • If you don't have a piping bag, you can make a small incision in the side of the doughnut with a knife and carefully spoon in the jam.
